stem: The moon does not fall to Earth because: (A) The net force on it is zero (B) It is beyond the pull of Earth’s gravity (C) It is being pulled by the Sun and planets as well as by Earth (D) The statement is wrong: the moon is in a state of free fall

An astronaut floating weightlessly in space shakes a large iron block rapidly back and forth, and compares it to moving it on a smooth horizontal surface on Earth. She finds that: (A) the shaking costs no effort because the block has no weight (B) the shaking costs some effort but considerably less than on Earth (C) although weightless, the effort required is the same (D) the shaking costs more effort than on Earth

A ball is thrown vertically upward. Observer A films the motion and plays the tape backwards (tape starts at the highest point and ends at the release point). Observer B watches from a frame moving at constant velocity equal to the ball’s initial velocity. The ball has a downward acceleration according to observer: (A) both A and B (B) only A (C) only B (D) neither

A block of mass m is placed on a smooth wedge of inclination θ. The whole system is accelerated horizontally so that the block does not slip on the wedge. The force exerted by the wedge on the block has magnitude: (A) mg (B) mg/cosθ (C) mg cosθ (D) mg tanθ

Ball A is released from rest when the spring is at its natural length. Ball A hangs over a pulley; the other side connects through a spring to block B (mass M) resting on the ground. For B to leave the ground at some instant, the minimum mass of A must be: (A) M/2 (B) M (C) 2M (D) A function of M and the spring constant k
A lift moves up with acceleration 3.675 m/s². The weight of a man (g = 10 m/s²): (A) increases by 36.75% (B) decreases by 37.5% (C) increases by 137.5% (D) remains the same

The linear momentum p vs time t curve for an object is an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve, steepest at t = t₀. Which is true? (A) Rate of change of momentum is highest at t = t₀ (B) Net force first increases then decreases (C) If it started from rest at t = 0, it has maximum velocity at t = t₀ (D) More than one option is true

Two smooth spheres, each radius 5 cm and weight w, rest one on the other inside a fixed smooth vertical cylinder of radius 8 cm. The reactions between the spheres and the vertical side of the cylinder are: (A) w/4 and 3w/4 (B) w/4 and w/4 (C) 3w/4 and 3w/4 (D) w and w

A trolley is pulled up a 15° incline by a man sitting on it, applying 250 N to a rope. As the figure shows, the rope runs from his hands up to a pulley fixed at the top of the incline, back down around a movable pulley attached to the trolley , and up again to an anchor — so three rope segments pull the system up the slope. Combined mass of man + trolley = 100 kg. The acceleration is [sin15° = 0.26, g = 10 m/s²]: (A) 2.4 m/s² (B) 4 m/s² (C) 4.9 m/s² (D) 0.1 m/s²

On a 37° incline (the “trolley”) a 5 kg block is connected over a pulley to a hanging block M; a 1 kg plumb bob on the block settles at 53° to the normal of the incline in the steady state. Find M: (A) 8 kg (B) 10 kg (C) 12 kg (D) 16 kg

A block in equilibrium is held by a horizontal string to a wall and a spring at 53° to the vertical (up to the ceiling). Find the block’s acceleration just after the string is burnt: (A) 3g/5 (B) 4g/5 (C) 4g/3 (D) None of these

Rods AC and BC are hinged at C; ends A and B slide on the ground with v₀ = 8 m/s and v₊ = 4√3 m/s. AC makes 60° and BC makes 30° with the ground. The speed of hinge C is: (A) √13 m/s (B) 2√13 m/s (C) 3√13 m/s (D) data insufficient
A car moving at 40 km/h is stopped by braking within 4.0 m. If the car weighs 2000 kg, the average force required is: (A) 3.1×10⁴ N (B) 4.1×10⁴ N (C) 5.1×10⁴ N (D) 1.1×10⁴ N

A triangular prism in gravity-free space has two 100 N forces applied normal to its two equal faces, each making 60° with the vertical axis of symmetry. The force needed to keep the prism in equilibrium is: (A) 50 N (B) 100 N (C) 150 N (D) 200 N
Three identical blocks A, B, C (each m = 2 kg) sit in a row C–B–A on a frictionless surface; F = 12 N pulls A. Find the tension in the string between B and C (in N).
A block on a smooth surface is acted on by 4 N horizontally and 3 N perpendicular to it. Find the resultant force on the block (in N).
Block A slides on the incline of a wedge with acceleration 5 m/s²; block B moves against the vertical face (37° wedge). If the acceleration of B is (4x/3) m/s², find x.

A block tied between two springs is in equilibrium. If upper spring is cut, then the acceleration of the block just after cut is 6 m/s² downwards. Now, if instead of upper spring, lower spring is cut, then the magnitude of acceleration of the block just after the cut will be (Take g = 10 m/s²) [figure: block m hangs vertically between one spring fixed to the ceiling above it and one spring fixed to the floor below it] (A) 16 m/s² (B) 4 m/s² (C) Cannot be determined (D) None of the above

Two masses each equal to m are lying on x-axis at (−a, 0) and (+a, 0), respectively. They are connected by a light string. A force F is applied at the origin (mid-point of the string) along vertical direction. As a result, the masses move towards each other without losing contact with ground. What is the acceleration of each mass? Assume the instantaneous position of the masses as (−x, 0) and (x, 0), respectively. (A) (2F/m)·√(a² − x²)/x (B) (2F/m)·x/√(a² − x²) (C) (F/2m)·x/√(a² − x²) (D) (F/m)·x/√(a² − x²)

Three masses M = 100 kg, m 1 = 10 kg and m 2 = 20 kg are arranged in a system as shown in figure (m 1 on top of M, string over a pulley at M's top corner, m 2 hanging against M's vertical face). All the surfaces are frictionless and strings are inextensible and weightless. The pulleys are also weightless and frictionless. A force F is applied on the system so that the mass m 2 moves upward with an acceleration of 2 m s −2 . The value of F is: (Take g = 10 m s −2 ) (A) 3360 N (B) 3380 N (C) 3120 N (D) 3240 N

System is shown in the figure (left wedge, inclined face at 30°, moving left at u m/s; right wedge with vertical face touching the cylinder, moving right at 2u m/s). Assume that cylinder remains in contact with the two wedges. The velocity of cylinder is (A) √(19 − 4√3)·u/2 m/s (B) √13 u/2 m/s (C) √3 u m/s (D) √7 u m/s

A man is raising himself and the crate on which he stands with an acceleration of 5 m s −2 by a massless rope-and-pulley arrangement. Mass of the man is 100 kg and that of the crate is 50 kg. If g = 10 m s −2 , then the tension in the rope is (A) 2250 N (B) 1125 N (C) 750 N (D) 375 N

Block B has mass m and is released from rest when it is on top of wedge A, which has mass 3m. Determine the tension in cord CD needed to hold the wedge from moving while B is sliding down A. Neglect friction. (Figure: wedge A of angle θ on rollers, tied by horizontal cord CD to a wall on the left.) (A) 2mg cosθ (B) (mg/2) cosθ (C) (mg/2) sin 2θ (D) (mg/2) sinθ

Figure shows two blocks, each of mass m. The system is released from rest. If accelerations of blocks A and B at any instant (not initially) are a 1 and a 2 respectively, then (B slides on the floor, its string rising at angle θ to a pulley; A hangs vertically from the pulley) (A) a 1 = a 2 cosθ (B) a 2 = a 1 cosθ (C) a 1 = a 2 (D) None of these

key: C reading in (a) is less than 8g and in (b) it is 8g
stem: Referring to figures (a) and (b): in each, a light pulley hangs from a spring balance fixed to the ceiling. In (a) blocks of 6 kg and 2 kg hang over the pulley; in (b) blocks of 4 kg and 4 kg. (A) reading of spring balance in (a) is 8 g and in (b) is also 8 g (B) reading in (a) is 8 g and in (b) it is less than 8 g (C) reading in (a) is less than 8 g and in (b) it is 8 g (D) reading in both (a) and (b) is less than 8 g

A block is kept on a smooth inclined plane of angle of inclination 30° that moves with a constant acceleration so that the block does not slide relative to the inclined plane. Let F 1 be the contact force between the block and the plane. Now the inclined plane stops and let F 2 be the contact force between the two in this case. Then F 1 /F 2 is (A) 1 (B) 4/3 (C) 2 (D) 3/2

The acceleration of the block of mass M in the situation shown in the figure is g/x; then x is ____. All the surfaces are frictionless. (M on a fixed 30° incline; string runs up over a pulley at the top, down under a movable pulley carrying 2M, and up to the ceiling.)

Block B starts from rest and accelerates as a B = 12t m s −2 . Simultaneously the other end of the string is pulled with constant acceleration a 0 . If at t = 3 s block A comes to rest, then the value of a 0 (in m s −2 ) is equal to ____. (String: from B on a horizontal ledge over a fixed pulley, down around the movable pulley carrying A, up over a second fixed pulley to the free end pulled horizontally.)

Three blocks are connected as shown in the figure, on a horizontal frictionless table. If m 1 = 1 kg, m 2 = 8 kg, m 3 = 27 kg and T 3 = 36 N, T 2 will be: [Figure: m 1 –T 1 – m 2 –T 2 – m 3 in a row, left to right; T 3 = 36 N pulls m 3 to the right.] (A) 18 N (B) 9 N (C) 3.375 N (D) 1.75 N

A monkey of mass 30 kg climbs a rope which can withstand a maximum tension of 360 N. The maximum acceleration which this rope can tolerate for the climbing of monkey is : (g = 10 m/s²) (A) 2 m/s² (B) 3 m/s² (C) 4 m/s² (D) 5 m/s²

A string of negligible mass going over a clamped pulley of mass m supports a block of M as shown in the figure. The force on the pulley by the clamp is given by [figure: the pulley is clamped to a vertical wall; the string runs horizontally from the wall over the top of the pulley and then hangs vertically down to the block M] (A) √2 Mg (B) √2 mg (C) (√((M + m)² + m²)) g (D) (√((M + m)² + M²)) g

A force F̄ = (−10î + 10ĵ) N acts on a 2 kg object initially at rest. Calculate the velocity of the object after 4 seconds. (A) v̄ = (−20î + 20ĵ) m/s (B) v̄ = (−10î + 20ĵ) m/s (C) v̄ = (−30î + 20ĵ) m/s (D) v̄ = (−20î + 40ĵ) m/s

Blocks A and C start from rest & move to the right with acceleration a A = 12t m/s² and a C = 3 m/s². Here ‘t’ is in seconds. The time when block B again comes to rest is : [Figure: A on the left ledge and C on the right ledge; one string runs from A over a fixed pulley, down around a movable pulley carrying B (hanging in the gap), up over a second fixed pulley to C.] (A) 1 s (B) 3/2 s (C) 2 s (D) 1/2 s

In the figure shown the relation between magnitudes of a A and a B is related as a A = n a B sinθ then n is [Figure: wedge B with incline angle θ moves on the horizontal floor; rod A, held in fixed guides, stays perpendicular (90°) to the inclined face and rests on it.]
